newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador budget proposes $5.57 billion spending.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador budget proposes $5.57 billion spending.

text.p: Ecuador's new government Wednesday sent to Congress its 1997 budget proposal, which foresees expenditure of 18.6 billion sucres ($5.57 billion), Economy Minister Pablo Concha said.
"The budget will be financed by the elimination of gas subsidies, elimination of exemptions on value added tax and a rise in value added tax," Concha told journalists.
This year's budget is 11.7 billion sucres ($3.5 billion).

The 1997 budget foresees that 44 percent of revenue will be used to cover debt servicing charges, down from 50 percent this year. The proposal anticipates that 20 percent of revenue will be used on education and 15 percent on investment.
Inflation is seen at 18 percent in 1997, according to the proposal, down from this year's 25 percent.z Economic growth is anticipated to rise to four percent next year from 2.9 percent in 1996.

Talking about the debt servicing costs, Concha said: "the only thing this government is doing is fulfilling the commitments of the previous administration. If we don't fulfill them, access to international credit will stop."
The minister added that the budget is based on an estimate of an average price of $16 per barrell of crude oil, compared with an estimate of $14.5 in this year's budget.
Ecuador's government has said next year's budget will include fiscal austerity measures.
The government is now in the final stages of preparing an economic program to be unveiled on November 16.
On Tuesday, President Abdala Bucaram, who took office last July, said the authorities were working on a plan to revalue the sucre against the U.S. dollar.
Congress has until the end of December to approve the budget.
